accentColor.label: Accent Color
accentColor.description: Utilities for controlling the accented color of a form control.
accentColor.notes: Accent color utilities control the accented color of form controls like checkboxes and radio buttons. They are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any accent color by adding a forward slash followed by a percentage value (0-100). For example, `accent-rose-500/50`. Note that setting accent color opacity has limited browser support (currently Firefox only).

alignContent.label: Align Content
alignContent.description: Utilities for controlling how rows are positioned in multi-row flex and grid containers.
alignContent.notes: This utility controls the spacing between and around content items along the cross-axis of a container. It only has an effect on multi-row or multi-column flex/grid containers. For single-line alignment, use 'Align Items' instead.

alignItems.label: Align Items
alignItems.description: Utilities for controlling how flex and grid items are positioned along a container's cross axis.
alignItems.notes: These utilities control how flex and grid items are positioned along a container's cross axis. They affect the alignment of items within a single line or row. For multi-row containers, use `align-content` instead. Includes `safe` variants for fallback behavior.

alignSelf.label: Align Self
alignSelf.description: Utilities for controlling how an individual flex or grid item is positioned along its container's cross axis.
alignSelf.notes: Aligns an individual flex or grid item along its container's cross axis. Options include `auto` (follows container's `align-items`), `start`, `end`, `center`, `stretch`, and `baseline`. The `safe` keyword variants (`self-end-safe`, `self-center-safe`) prevent content from overflowing. `self-baseline` aligns the first line of text, while `self-baseline-last` aligns the last line, useful for text alignment in varying height elements.

animation.label: Animation
animation.description: Utilities for animating elements with CSS animations.
animation.notes: Applies CSS animations to elements. Includes predefined animations: `spin` (for loading), `ping` (for notifications), `pulse` (for skeleton loaders), and `bounce` (for indicators). Use `animate-none` to disable animation. Supports custom CSS animations via arbitrary values, where you can define properties like `name duration timing-function delay iteration-count direction fill-mode play-state`. Conditionally apply animations using `motion-safe` and `motion-reduce` variants to respect user preferences for reduced motion.

appearance.label: Appearance
appearance.description: Utilities for suppressing native form control styling.
appearance.notes: Use `appearance-none` to reset browser-specific styling on elements, which is useful when creating custom form components. Use `appearance-auto` to restore default browser styling, often for accessibility modes.

aspectRatio.label: Aspect Ratio
aspectRatio.description: Utilities for controlling the aspect ratio of an element.
aspectRatio.notes:
Sets the preferred aspect ratio for an element. This is useful for sizing videos or images. 
- Use keywords like `square` (1/1) and `video` (16/9). 
- For arbitrary ratios, use the format `width/height` inside the brackets, for example `[4/3]`.

backdropBlur.label: Backdrop Blur
backdropBlur.description: Utilities for applying backdrop blur filters to an element.
backdropBlur.notes:
Applies a blur filter to the backdrop of an element.
- Values are typically expressed in `px` and are sourced from your theme's `blur` scale.
- Use `backdrop-blur-none` to disable the blur.
- Supports arbitrary length values (e.g., `[5px]`, `[0.5rem]`) and custom CSS properties (e.g., `[var(--my-blur-amount)]`).

backdropBrightness.label: Backdrop Brightness
backdropBrightness.description: Utilities for applying backdrop brightness filters to an element.
backdropBrightness.notes: Controls the brightness of an element's backdrop. Values are typically percentages (e.g., `backdrop-brightness-50` for 50%). For arbitrary values, you can use decimals or other CSS units like `backdrop-brightness-[1.75]` or `backdrop-brightness-[200%]`.

backdropContrast.label: Backdrop Contrast
backdropContrast.description: Utilities for applying backdrop contrast filters to an element.
backdropContrast.notes: Controls the contrast of an element's backdrop. Values are typically percentages. `100` is normal, `0` removes all contrast, and values above `100` increase contrast. Supports arbitrary values, e.g., `backdrop-contrast-[.75]` (for 75%) or `backdrop-contrast-[150%]`.

backdropGrayscale.label: Backdrop Grayscale
backdropGrayscale.description: Utilities for applying backdrop grayscale filters to an element.
backdropGrayscale.notes: Applies a grayscale filter to an element's backdrop. Default values are numeric percentages (0-100). `backdrop-grayscale` is equivalent to `backdrop-grayscale-100`. Use `backdrop-grayscale-0` for no effect. Supports arbitrary values, which can be unitless numbers (0-1, e.g., `-[0.5]`) or percentages (e.g., `-[75%]` for 75%).

backdropHueRotate.label: Backdrop Hue Rotate
backdropHueRotate.description: Utilities for applying backdrop hue-rotate filters to an element.
backdropHueRotate.notes: Rotates the hue of an element's backdrop. Default unit is degrees (`deg`). Use negative values for counter-clockwise rotation (e.g., `-backdrop-hue-rotate-90`). For arbitrary values, other units like `rad` or `turn` can be specified (e.g., `-[3.142rad]`).

backdropInvert.label: Backdrop Invert
backdropInvert.description: Utilities for applying backdrop invert filters to an element.
backdropInvert.notes: Applies an invert filter to the backdrop of an element. `backdrop-invert` applies a 100% invert, while `backdrop-invert-0` removes the filter. Numbered utilities like `backdrop-invert-65` correspond to percentages.

backdropOpacity.label: Backdrop Opacity
backdropOpacity.description: Utilities for applying backdrop opacity filters to an element.
backdropOpacity.notes: Controls the opacity of all backdrop filters applied to an element. Values can be percentages (0-100) from the default scale or arbitrary values, including fractional numbers (e.g., `0.15`) or specific percentages (e.g., `50%`).

backdropSaturate.label: Backdrop Saturate
backdropSaturate.description: Utilities for applying backdrop saturation filters to an element.
backdropSaturate.notes: Controls the saturation of the backdrop of an element. Values represent a percentage; 0% is completely desaturated (grayscale), and 100% is the original saturation. Values over 100% will over-saturate the image. Arbitrary values can be used to set specific percentages, e.g., `backdrop-saturate-[.25]` for 25%.

backdropSepia.label: Backdrop Sepia
backdropSepia.description: Utilities for applying backdrop sepia filters to an element.
backdropSepia.notes: Applies a sepia filter to an element's backdrop. The default `backdrop-sepia` utility applies a 100% sepia filter. Numeric utilities like `backdrop-sepia-50` apply a percentage filter. Use arbitrary values for custom percentages or other valid CSS values (e.g., `backdrop-sepia-[75%]` or `backdrop-sepia-[.25]`).

backdropFilter.label: Backdrop Filter
backdropFilter.description: Utilities for applying backdrop filters to an element.
backdropFilter.notes: Utilities for applying backdrop filters to an element. These filters apply to the area behind an element, allowing you to create frosted glass effects, blurred backgrounds, etc. You can combine various backdrop filter utilities (e.g., blur, brightness, grayscale, hue-rotate, invert, opacity, saturate, sepia). Use `backdrop-filter-none` to remove all applied backdrop filters. Arbitrary values can be any valid CSS filter function, such as `blur(10px) contrast(1.2)` or `url('filters.svg#filter-id')`.

backfaceVisibility.label: Backface Visibility
backfaceVisibility.description: Utilities for controlling if an element's backface is visible.
backfaceVisibility.notes: Determines whether the reverse side of an element is visible when it faces the user during a 3D transformation. Use `backface-hidden` to make the backface invisible, and `backface-visible` to keep it visible.

backgroundAttachment.label: Background Attachment
backgroundAttachment.description: Utilities for controlling how a background image behaves when scrolling.
backgroundAttachment.notes: The `bg-fixed` utility fixes the background image relative to the viewport. `bg-local` scrolls the background image with its container and the viewport. `bg-scroll` scrolls the background image with the viewport, but not with its container.

backgroundBlendMode.label: Background Blend Mode
backgroundBlendMode.description: Utilities for controlling how an element's background image should blend with its background color.
backgroundBlendMode.notes: These utilities allow you to control how an element's background image interacts and blends with its background color, using various CSS blend modes.

backgroundClip.label: Background Clip
backgroundClip.description: Utilities for controlling the bounding box of an element's background.
backgroundClip.notes: Controls how an element's background extends into its border, padding, or content box. The `bg-clip-text` utility crops the background to the shape of the text, often used with gradients.

backgroundColor.label: Background Color
backgroundColor.description: Utilities for controlling an element's background color.
backgroundColor.notes: Background color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any background color by adding a forward slash followed by a percentage value (0-100). For example, `bg-red-500/50` applies a 50% opacity to the red-500 color.

backgroundImage.label: Background Image
backgroundImage.description: Utilities for controlling an element's background image.
backgroundImage.notes: This utility controls an element's background image, supporting various types including plain images from URLs, and linear, radial, and conic gradients. For gradients, you can specify directions, angles (with negative support for linear/conic), and define color stops using `from-`, `via-`, `to-` utilities. You can also specify precise stop positions (e.g., `from-50%`). By default, gradients interpolate in the `oklab` color space. Use `bg-none` to remove a background image.

valueSets.typeHint: url | gradient | color | percentage | angle | position | custom-property

backgroundOrigin.label: Background Origin
backgroundOrigin.description: Utilities for controlling how an element's background is positioned relative to borders, padding, and content.
backgroundOrigin.notes:
Controls the positioning area of an element's background image. Options include: 
- `bg-origin-border`: The background starts at the outside edge of the border. 
- `bg-origin-padding`: The background starts at the outside edge of the padding. This is the CSS default. 
- `bg-origin-content`: The background starts at the outside edge of the content box.

backgroundPosition.label: Background Position
backgroundPosition.description: Utilities for controlling the position of an element's background image.
backgroundPosition.notes: Use utilities like `bg-center`, `bg-right`, and `bg-top-left` to control the position of an element's background image. For custom values, use `bg-position-[<value>]` with arbitrary position values like `center top 1rem`.

backgroundRepeat.label: Background Repeat
backgroundRepeat.description: Utilities for controlling the repetition of an element's background image.
backgroundRepeat.notes: Controls how a background image repeats within an element. Options include repeating both horizontally and vertically (`bg-repeat`), only horizontally (`bg-repeat-x`), only vertically (`bg-repeat-y`), repeating without clipping and distributing remaining space (`bg-repeat-space`), repeating without clipping by stretching (`bg-repeat-round`), or preventing repetition entirely (`bg-no-repeat`).

backgroundSize.label: Background Size
backgroundSize.description: Utilities for controlling the background size of an element's background image.
backgroundSize.notes: Control the size of an element's background image. Use `bg-cover` to scale the image to fill the container (cropping if necessary). Use `bg-contain` to scale the image to the outer edges without cropping. Use `bg-auto` to display the image at its default size. Arbitrary values allow for complex size definitions like `auto_100px`.

borderCollapse.label: Border Collapse
borderCollapse.description: Utilities for controlling whether table borders should collapse or be separated.
borderCollapse.notes: Controls whether table borders are merged (`collapse`) or rendered individually (`separate`). The `border-collapse` utility merges adjacent cell borders, while `border-separate` forces each cell to display its own distinct borders. These utilities apply to the `<table>` element.

borderColor.label: Border Color
borderColor.description: Utilities for controlling the color of an element's borders.
borderColor.notes: Border color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any border color using a forward slash followed by a percentage (0-100), e.g., `border-red-500/50`. Utilities are available for all sides, individual sides (like `border-t-`), horizontal/vertical sides (like `border-x-`), and logical properties (like `border-s-`). The `divide-` utility applies border colors between child elements.

borderRadius.label: Border Radius
borderRadius.description: Utilities for controlling the border radius of an element.
borderRadius.notes: Apply border radii to all corners, individual sides (e.g., `rounded-t-md`), or specific corners (e.g., `rounded-tl-lg`). Supports logical properties (e.g., `rounded-s-md`). Use `rounded-full` for pill shapes and `rounded-none` to remove radii. Custom values can be defined (e.g., `rounded-[2vw]`).

borderSpacing.label: Border Spacing
borderSpacing.description: Utilities for controlling the spacing between table borders.
borderSpacing.notes: Controls the spacing between borders of table cells. It requires `border-collapse: separate` to have an effect. You can apply uniform spacing, or independent horizontal (`x`) and vertical (`y`) spacing. Custom values are supported.

borderStyle.label: Border Style
borderStyle.description: Utilities for controlling the style of an element's borders.
borderStyle.notes: Controls the style of an element's borders, such as solid, dashed, or dotted. `border-none` can be used to remove borders, especially for responsive adjustments. Divide utilities (`divide-solid`, `divide-dashed`) control the border style between child elements.

borderWidth.label: Border Width
borderWidth.description: Utilities for controlling the width of an element's borders.
borderWidth.notes: Set the border width for all sides or specific sides of an element using utilities like `border-2` or `border-t-4`. For horizontal or vertical pairs, use `border-x-4` or `border-y-4`. Logical properties `border-s` (inline-start) and `border-e` (inline-end) adapt to text direction. Use `divide-x` and `divide-y` to add borders between child elements. For reversed element order (e.g., `flex-row-reverse`), apply `divide-x-reverse` or `divide-y-reverse` utilities to correctly position the borders.

boxDecorationBreak.label: Box Decoration Break
boxDecorationBreak.description: Utilities for controlling how element fragments should be rendered across multiple lines, columns, or pages.
boxDecorationBreak.notes: This utility controls how properties like background, border, and padding are rendered when an element breaks across multiple lines or columns. `box-decoration-clone` treats each fragment as a distinct box, while `box-decoration-slice` renders them as one continuous entity.

boxShadow.label: Box Shadow
boxShadow.description: Utilities for controlling the box shadow of an element.
boxShadow.notes: Tailwind provides utilities for outer and inset box shadows, and for outer and inset rings. Shadows come in predefined sizes like `shadow-md` and `inset-shadow-sm`. Rings have widths like `ring-2`. You can customize colors with theme values (e.g., `shadow-blue-500`) or using opacity modifiers (e.g., `/50`). Use `shadow-none`, `inset-shadow-none`, `ring-0`, or `inset-ring-0` to remove existing effects. Custom CSS values are supported, for example, `shadow-[0_35px_35px_rgba(0,0,0,0.25)]` or `shadow-[var(--my-shadow)]`.

boxSizing.label: Box Sizing
boxSizing.description: Utilities for controlling how the browser should calculate an element's total size.
boxSizing.notes:
Controls how the browser calculates an element's total size. 
- `box-border`: Sets `box-sizing: border-box`, making the element's width/height include borders and padding. For example, a 100px x 100px element with 2px border and 4px padding will render as 100px x 100px, with its content area being 88px x 88px. This is Tailwind's default behavior via preflight. 
- `box-content`: Sets `box-sizing: content-box`, adding borders and padding on top of the element's specified width/height. For example, a 100px x 100px element with 2px border and 4px padding will render as 112px x 112px, with its content area being 100px x 100px.

breakAfter.label: Break After
breakAfter.description: Utilities for controlling how a column or page should break after an element.
breakAfter.notes: Use utilities like `break-after-column` and `break-after-page` to control how a column or page break should behave after an element.

breakBefore.label: Break Before
breakBefore.description: Utilities for controlling how a column or page should break before an element.
breakBefore.notes: Controls how a column or page break should behave *before* an element. Common options include `break-before-column` to force a column break, or `break-before-page` to force a page break. Use `break-before-auto` for default browser behavior and `break-before-avoid` to prevent breaks.

breakInside.label: Break Inside
breakInside.description: Utilities for controlling how a column or page should break within an element.
breakInside.notes: Controls whether an element should be broken across columns, pages, or regions. Use `avoid` to prevent any breaks, or more specific `avoid-page` or `avoid-column` options.

captionSide.label: Caption Side
captionSide.description: Utilities for controlling the alignment of a caption element inside of a table.
captionSide.notes: Positions the caption element at either the top or bottom of a table, controlling the `caption-side` CSS property.

caretColor.label: Caret Color
caretColor.description: Utilities for controlling the color of the text input cursor.
caretColor.notes: Caret color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can use any of your defined colors. For custom colors, use arbitrary values. Opacity modifiers (e.g., `caret-red-500/50`) are also supported.

clear.label: Clear
clear.description: Utilities for controlling the wrapping of content around an element.
clear.notes: Utilities for controlling how elements wrap around floats. `clear-left` clears left floats, `clear-right` clears right floats, and `clear-both` clears both. `clear-start` and `clear-end` are logical properties that adapt to text direction. `clear-none` disables clearing.

colorScheme.label: Color Scheme
colorScheme.description: Utilities for controlling the color scheme of an element.
colorScheme.notes: Controls the preferred color scheme for an element, affecting how form controls, scrollbars, and system colors are rendered. These utilities react to the user's system color scheme setting. Can be combined with dark mode variants (e.g., `dark:scheme-dark`).

textColor.label: Text Color
textColor.description: Utilities for controlling the text color of an element.
textColor.notes: Text color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any text color by adding a forward slash followed by a percentage value (0-100), e.g., `text-red-500/50`. Arbitrary values like `text-[#bada55]` or CSS variables like `text-[var(--my-color)]` are also supported.

columns.label: Columns
columns.description: Utilities for controlling the number of columns within an element.
columns.notes: Controls the number of columns or the ideal column width for an element's content. Use `columns-<number>` for a fixed column count (e.g., `columns-3`). Use `columns-<size>` for an ideal column width (e.g., `columns-xs`), allowing the number of columns to adjust automatically. Supports arbitrary values for custom counts or widths, including CSS variables.

content.label: Content
content.description: Utilities for controlling the content of the before and after pseudo-elements.
content.notes: Utilities for setting the `content` property of `::before` and `::after` pseudo-elements. Supports arbitrary values for strings (e.g., `content-['Hello_World']`), attribute references (e.g., `content-[attr(data-title)]`), or CSS variables (e.g., `content-(--my-content)`). When using strings, replace spaces with underscores and escape literal underscores with a backslash.

cursor.label: Cursor
cursor.description: Utilities for controlling the cursor style when hovering over an element.
cursor.notes: Set the cursor style when hovering over an element using keywords like `pointer`, `wait`, or `not-allowed`. You can also provide arbitrary CSS cursor values, including `url()` functions or custom properties, using bracket notation.

fieldSizing.label: Field Sizing
fieldSizing.description: Utilities for controlling the sizing of form controls.
fieldSizing.notes: Controls the sizing of form controls. Use `field-sizing-content` to allow a form control to adjust its size based on content. Use `field-sizing-fixed` to make a form control use a fixed size. Try typing in the examples to observe the effect.

fill.label: Fill
fill.description: Utilities for styling the fill of SVG elements.
fill.notes: Fill color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. Use `fill-current` to set the fill color to the current text color. For custom values, use arbitrary color syntax or CSS variables.

blur.label: Blur
blur.description: Utilities for applying blur filters to an element.
blur.notes: Utilities for applying blur filters to an element. Tailwind provides a default scale for blur radii (e.g., `blur-sm`, `blur-lg`). Use `blur-none` to remove a blur. Arbitrary values like `blur-[10px]` are also supported, and can use CSS length units.

brightness.label: Brightness
brightness.description: Utilities for applying brightness filters to an element.
brightness.notes: Applies a brightness filter to an element, adjusting its luminosity. Default values are interpreted as percentages (e.g., `brightness-100` means 100% normal brightness, `brightness-50` means 50% darker). Values above 100 (e.g., `brightness-125`) increase brightness. Supports arbitrary values for precise control, which can be unitless numbers (e.g., `[1.75]`) or percentages (e.g., `[175%]`).

contrast.label: Contrast
contrast.description: Utilities for applying contrast filters to an element.
contrast.notes: Adjusts the contrast of an element's colors. Values are typically percentages: `100` is normal contrast, `0` is fully desaturated, and values above `100` increase contrast. Supports arbitrary values, which can be specified as numbers or percentages (e.g., `contrast-[1.5]` or `contrast-[200%]` for 150% or 200% contrast respectively).

dropShadow.label: Drop Shadow
dropShadow.description: Utilities for applying drop-shadow filters to an element.
dropShadow.notes: Applies a drop-shadow filter, primarily for irregular shapes like text and SVG (use `box-shadow` for regular elements). Default opacities are low; increase with `/` (e.g., `drop-shadow-xl/50`) for a stronger effect. Customize color using `drop-shadow-<color>` (e.g., `drop-shadow-indigo-500/50`). Use `drop-shadow-none` to remove. Supports arbitrary CSS shadow values like `drop-shadow-[0_35px_35px_rgba(0,0,0,0.25)]`.

grayscale.label: Grayscale
grayscale.description: Utilities for applying grayscale filters to an element.
grayscale.notes: Controls the intensity of the grayscale filter applied to an element. The `grayscale` class applies a 100% grayscale effect. Numeric utilities like `grayscale-25` apply a specific percentage (e.g., 25%). Arbitrary values can be a unitless number (0-1) or a percentage (0%-100%).

hueRotate.label: Hue Rotate
hueRotate.description: Utilities for applying hue-rotate filters to an element.
hueRotate.notes:
Rotates the hue of an element by a specified number of degrees. 
- Default unit is degrees (`deg`).
- Use negative values for counter-clockwise rotation (e.g., `-hue-rotate-45`).
- Arbitrary values can use other units like `rad`, `grad`, or `turn`.

invert.label: Invert
invert.description: Utilities for applying invert filters to an element.
invert.notes: Controls the color inversion of an element. The `invert` class applies 100% inversion. Numeric values like `invert-20` apply a percentage. Arbitrary values can be used for precise control, including custom properties.

saturate.label: Saturate Filter
saturate.description: Utilities for applying saturation filters to an element.
saturate.notes: Controls the saturation of an element's colors. Values are typically percentages, where `100` means no change, `0` means completely desaturated (grayscale), and values above `100` increase saturation. Arbitrary values can be used to set specific percentages (e.g., `[75%]`) or unitless numbers (e.g., `[.75]` for 75% saturation).

sepia.label: Sepia
sepia.description: Utilities for applying sepia filters to an element.
sepia.notes: Applies a sepia filter to an element. Use `sepia` for 100% sepia, or `sepia-0` and `sepia-50` for partial effects. Arbitrary values like `sepia-[.25]` can be used for custom amounts, where `.25` means 25% sepia.

filter.label: Filter
filter.description: Utilities for applying filters to an element.
filter.notes: The `filter` utility controls whether an element should be rendered with any graphical filters. It acts as an enabling switch for other filter utilities like `blur`, `grayscale`, etc. Use `filter-none` to remove all applied filters. You can also specify arbitrary CSS filter functions directly using `filter-[<value>]` (e.g., `filter-[url('filters.svg#filter-id')]`) or apply a custom property using `filter-(<custom-property>)`.

flexBasis.label: Flex Basis
flexBasis.description: Utilities for controlling the initial size of flex items.
flexBasis.notes: Sets the initial main size of a flex item before any available space is distributed. This determines the size of the item relative to other items in the flex container. Numeric values (e.g., `basis-64`) correspond to the `spacing` scale, fractional values (e.g., `basis-1/2`) represent percentages, and named values (e.g., `basis-xs`) reference the `container` scale. You can also use arbitrary values or custom CSS properties.

flexDirection.label: Flex Direction
flexDirection.description: Utilities for controlling the direction of flex items.
flexDirection.notes: Controls the primary axis and direction of flex items within a flex container. `flex-row` arranges items horizontally, while `flex-col` arranges them vertically. Adding `-reverse` to either will reverse the order of the items.

flexGrow.label: Flex Grow
flexGrow.description: Utilities for controlling how flex items grow.
flexGrow.notes: Utilities to control how flex items grow to fill available space. The `grow` utility sets `flex-grow: 1`. Use `grow-0` to prevent items from growing. You can set proportional growth using `grow-<number>` utilities (e.g., `grow-3`, `grow-7`) or provide any custom numeric value with `grow-[<value>]` or a custom CSS property with `grow-(<custom-property>)`.

flexShrink.label: Flex Shrink
flexShrink.description: Utilities for controlling how flex items shrink.
flexShrink.notes:
Controls how a flex item shrinks relative to other flex items within a flex container. 
- `shrink` (equivalent to `flex-shrink: 1`) allows the item to shrink if needed. 
- `shrink-0` (equivalent to `flex-shrink: 0`) prevents the item from shrinking. 
- Values are unitless numbers representing a shrink factor. 
- Supports arbitrary values (e.g., `shrink-[0.5]`) and CSS variables (e.g., `shrink-(--custom-factor)`).

flexWrap.label: Flex Wrap
flexWrap.description: Utilities for controlling how flex items wrap.
flexWrap.notes: Controls how flex items wrap within their container. Use `flex-nowrap` to prevent wrapping, `flex-wrap` to allow normal wrapping, and `flex-wrap-reverse` to wrap items in the opposite direction.

flex.label: Flex
flex.description: Utilities for controlling how flex items both grow and shrink.
flex.notes:
Controls how a flex item grows and shrinks, along with its initial size. Key utilities: 
- `flex-1`: Allows the item to grow and shrink as needed, ignoring its initial size. 
- `flex-initial`: Allows the item to shrink but not grow, respecting its initial size. 
- `flex-auto`: Allows the item to grow and shrink, respecting its initial size. 
- `flex-none`: Prevents the item from growing or shrinking. 
- Use custom values for the full `flex` shorthand property, e.g., `flex-[3_1_auto]` for `flex: 3 1 auto;`.

float.label: Float
float.description: Utilities for controlling the wrapping of content around an element.
float.notes: Floats an element to the left, right, start, or end of its container. `float-start` and `float-end` use logical properties to adapt to text direction. `float-none` removes any applied float.

fontFamily.label: Font Family
fontFamily.description: Utilities for controlling the font family of an element.
fontFamily.notes: Tailwind provides `font-sans`, `font-serif`, and `font-mono` utilities which map to default font stacks defined in your theme. You can extend these or add new font families by customizing your `tailwind.config.js` theme configuration. For custom fonts, use the `@font-face` CSS rule, and ensure `@import` statements for fonts are at the very top of your CSS file, before `@import 'tailwindcss'`.

options.label: Serif (ui-serif, Georgia, Cambria, 'Times New Roman', Times, serif)

fontSize.label: Font Size
fontSize.description: Utilities for controlling the font size of an element.
fontSize.notes: Sets the font size of an element. Predefined sizes like `text-sm` are available. Font size and line-height can be combined (e.g., `text-sm/6`). Arbitrary values such as `text-[14px]` or custom properties (`text-(length:--text-size)`) are supported. Theme customization allows setting default `line-height`, `letter-spacing`, and `font-weight` for font sizes.

fontStretch.label: Font Stretch
fontStretch.description: Utilities for selecting the width of a font face.
fontStretch.notes: Controls the width of a font face. This only applies to fonts that have multiple width variations available, otherwise the browser selects the closest match. You can use keywords like `normal`, `condensed`, or `expanded`, as well as percentage values (e.g., `font-stretch-50%`) or arbitrary values.

display.label: Display
display.description: Utilities for controlling the display box type of an element.
display.notes: Controls the display box type of an element. Includes `inline`, `block`, `flex`, `grid`, and `table` display types. `flow-root` creates a new block formatting context. `contents` makes children direct descendants of the parent. `hidden` removes elements from the document. `sr-only` hides an element visually but keeps it accessible to screen readers; `not-sr-only` reverses this for responsive design.

fontSmoothing.label: Font Smoothing
fontSmoothing.description: Utilities for controlling the font smoothing of an element.
fontSmoothing.notes: Controls the font smoothing of text. Use `antialiased` for grayscale antialiasing, and `subpixel-antialiased` for subpixel antialiasing.

fontStyle.label: Font Style
fontStyle.description: Utilities for controlling the style of text.
fontStyle.notes: Use the `italic` utility to make text italic. Use `not-italic` to display text normally.

fontVariantNumeric.label: Font Variant Numeric
fontVariantNumeric.description: Utilities for controlling the variant of numbers.
fontVariantNumeric.notes: Controls various numeric font features like `ordinal` glyphs (e.g., '1st'), `slashed-zero` for distinct zeros, `lining-nums` and `oldstyle-nums` for vertical alignment, `proportional-nums` and `tabular-nums` for spacing, and `diagonal-fractions` or `stacked-fractions` for fraction display. These utilities can be combined to apply multiple features, and `normal-nums` resets them.

fontWeight.label: Font Weight
fontWeight.description: Utilities for controlling the font weight of an element.
fontWeight.notes: Set the font weight of an element using utilities like `font-thin` (100) to `font-black` (900). You can also use arbitrary numeric values like `font-[550]` or CSS variables like `font-(var(--my-font-weight))`.

forcedColorAdjust.label: Forced Color Adjust
forcedColorAdjust.description: Utilities for opting in and out of forced colors.
forcedColorAdjust.notes:
Utilities to control if an element should adapt to a user's forced color mode (e.g., Windows High Contrast Mode).
- Use `forced-color-adjust-none` to opt an element out, preserving its original colors and styles.
- Use `forced-color-adjust-auto` to ensure the element adheres to colors enforced by forced colors mode.
- These utilities can be combined with the `forced-colors` variant for conditional styling.

gap.label: Gap
gap.description: Utilities for controlling gutters between grid and flexbox items.
gap.notes: Controls the gutters between grid and flexbox items. Use `gap-<number>` for both row and column gaps, or `gap-x-<number>` and `gap-y-<number>` for independent control. Supports custom values like `[10vw]`.

gridAutoColumns.label: Grid Auto Columns
gridAutoColumns.description: Utilities for controlling the size of implicitly-created grid columns.
gridAutoColumns.notes: Controls the size of grid columns that are implicitly created when there are more grid items than explicitly defined columns. For custom sizes, use arbitrary values like `[100px]` or `[minmax(0,2fr)]`.

gridAutoFlow.label: Grid Auto Flow
gridAutoFlow.description: Utilities for controlling how elements in a grid are auto-placed.
gridAutoFlow.notes: Controls how the auto-placement algorithm works for grid items. Use `grid-flow-row` to fill rows first, `grid-flow-col` to fill columns first. Add `dense` to try and fill any holes in the grid.

gridAutoRows.label: Grid Auto Rows
gridAutoRows.description: Utilities for controlling the size of implicitly-created grid rows.
gridAutoRows.notes: Controls the size of implicitly-created grid rows. Use keywords like `auto`, `min-content`, `max-content`, and `fraction` units. Arbitrary values can be specified using `[]` for precise control, including CSS functions like `minmax()`.

gridColumn.label: Grid Column
gridColumn.description: Utilities for controlling how elements are sized and placed across grid columns.
gridColumn.notes: Controls how grid items span, start, and end within grid columns. You can specify a starting line, ending line, or the number of columns to span. Combine `col-span` with `col-start` or `col-end` for precise placement. For arbitrary values, use bracket notation, for example `col-span-[2]` or `col-[2_/_span_2]`.

gridRow.label: Grid Row
gridRow.description: Utilities for controlling how elements are sized and placed across grid rows.
gridRow.notes: Controls how an element is sized and placed across grid rows. Use `row-span-<number>` to make an element span a specific number of rows (e.g., `row-span-2`). Use `row-start-<number>` or `row-end-<number>` to position an element at the nth grid line (e.g., `row-start-2`, `row-end-3`). Negative numbers are supported for `row`, `row-start`, and `row-end` to count from the end of the grid. Utilities can be combined, such as `row-span-2 row-start-2`.

gridTemplateColumns.label: Grid Template Columns
gridTemplateColumns.description: Utilities for specifying the columns in a grid layout.
gridTemplateColumns.notes: Use `grid-cols-<number>` utilities to create grids with _n_ equally sized columns. The `grid-cols-subgrid` utility allows an element to inherit the column tracks from its parent. For complex layouts, use arbitrary values to specify custom track lists.

gridTemplateRows.label: Grid Template Rows
gridTemplateRows.description: Utilities for specifying the rows in a grid layout.
gridTemplateRows.notes: Utilities like `grid-rows-2` create grids with _n_ equally sized rows. The `grid-rows-subgrid` utility adopts row tracks defined by the item's parent. For custom or complex row definitions, use arbitrary values, for example, `grid-rows-[200px_minmax(900px,1fr)_100px]`.

height.label: Height
height.description: Utilities for setting the height of an element.
height.notes: Set an element's height using the spacing scale (e.g., `h-24`), percentages (`h-1/2`), or various viewport units (`h-screen`, `h-dvh`, `h-lvh`, `h-svh`). The `size-` utilities (e.g., `size-16`, `size-full`, `size-dvw`) allow setting both width and height with a single class. Supports arbitrary values like `h-[128px]` or CSS variables like `h-[var(--custom-height)]`.

hyphens.label: Hyphens
hyphens.description: Utilities for controlling how words should be hyphenated.
hyphens.notes: Controls how words are hyphenated. `hyphens-none` prevents hyphenation, even with soft hyphens (`­`). `hyphens-manual` enables hyphenation only at explicit soft hyphens, which is the default browser behavior. `hyphens-auto` allows the browser to automatically choose hyphenation points based on language, while still prioritizing explicit soft hyphens.

isolation.label: Isolation
isolation.description: Utilities for controlling whether an element should explicitly create a new stacking context.
isolation.notes: Controls whether an element explicitly creates a new stacking context. This affects how z-index and blend modes behave within that element. `isolate` creates a new stacking context, while `isolation-auto` allows the default behavior, where a new stacking context is only created when necessary (e.g., due to z-index values, transforms, or filters).

justifyContent.label: Justify Content
justifyContent.description: Utilities for controlling how flex and grid items are positioned along a container's main axis.
justifyContent.notes: Controls the distribution of space between and around content items along the main axis. `safe` keywords (e.g., `justify-center-safe`) ensure items align to the start of the container when space is insufficient, preventing content overflow.

justifyItems.label: Justify Items
justifyItems.description: Utilities for controlling how grid items are aligned along their inline axis.
justifyItems.notes: Controls how grid items are aligned along their inline axis within their grid area. When there is not enough space available, the `justify-items-end-safe` utility will align items to the start of the container instead of the end. Similarly, `justify-items-center-safe` will align items to the start if space is insufficient.

justifySelf.label: Justify Self
justifySelf.description: Utilities for controlling how an individual grid item is aligned along its inline axis.
justifySelf.notes: Controls the alignment of an individual grid item along its inline axis. `justify-self-auto` aligns based on the container's `justify-items` property. `*-safe` variants (like `center-safe` or `end-safe`) will align items to the start of the container if there is insufficient space.

letterSpacing.label: Letter Spacing
letterSpacing.description: Utilities for controlling the tracking, or letter spacing, of an element.
letterSpacing.notes:
Utilities for controlling the tracking, or letter spacing, of an element. Tailwind provides a default scale with values like `tight` and `wide`.
- To apply negative letter spacing, prefix the class with a dash (e.g., `-tracking-2`). This is particularly useful if you've customized your theme to include numeric letter spacing values.
- You can use arbitrary values like `tracking-[0.25em]` or custom CSS properties like `tracking-(--my-tracking)`.

lineClamp.label: Line Clamp
lineClamp.description: Utilities for clamping text to a specific number of lines.
lineClamp.notes: Truncates multi-line text after a specific number of lines. Use `line-clamp-none` to remove the effect. Supports arbitrary values for custom line counts.

lineHeight.label: Line Height
lineHeight.description: Utilities for controlling the leading, or line height, of an element.
lineHeight.notes: Control line height using `leading-*` utilities. Use `leading-none` to set line height equal to font size. Line height can also be combined with font size using `text-sm/6` syntax. Arbitrary values can be a unitless number, a length (e.g., `20px`), or a CSS variable.

listStyleImage.label: List Style Image
listStyleImage.description: Utilities for controlling the marker images for list items.
listStyleImage.notes: Utilities for controlling the marker images for list items. Use `list-image-[<value>]` for arbitrary image URLs (e.g., `url('/img/checkmark.png')`), or `list-image-(<custom-property>)` for CSS variables (e.g., `(--my-list-image)`). Use `list-image-none` to remove the marker image.

listStylePosition.label: List Style Position
listStylePosition.description: Utilities for controlling the position of bullets and numbers in lists.
listStylePosition.notes: Use utilities like `list-inside` and `list-outside` to control the position of the markers and text indentation in a list.

listStyleType.label: List Style Type
listStyleType.description: Utilities for controlling the marker style of a list.
listStyleType.notes: Controls the marker style of list items. Use keywords like `disc`, `decimal`, and `none`. For custom styles, use arbitrary values in brackets, for example `list-[upper-roman]`.

margin.label: Margin
margin.description: Utilities for controlling an element's margin.
margin.notes: Utilities to control an element's margin. This includes `m-` for all sides, `mx-` for horizontal, `my-` for vertical, `mt-`/`mr-`/`mb-`/`ml-` for individual sides, and `ms-`/`me-` for logical inline start/end margins. Supports negative values by prefixing with a dash (e.g., `-mt-8`). `space-x-` and `space-y-` utilities add margin between child elements; use `space-x-reverse` or `space-y-reverse` for reversed child order. Space utilities are for simple flex layouts and have limitations with complex grids or wrapping content, where `gap` utilities or direct child margin/padding might be better. They are not designed to work with `divide` utilities.

maskClip.label: Mask Clip
maskClip.description: Utilities for controlling the bounding box of an element's mask.
maskClip.notes: Controls the bounding box of an element's mask, defining which part of the element the mask should be applied to. Use utilities like `mask-clip-border`, `mask-clip-padding`, and `mask-clip-content` to define the mask's boundary.

maskComposite.label: Mask Composite
maskComposite.description: Utilities for controlling how multiple masks are combined together.
maskComposite.notes: Use utilities like `mask-add` and `mask-intersect` to control how an element's masks are combined together.

maskImage.label: Mask Image
maskImage.description: Utilities for controlling an element's mask image.
maskImage.notes: Applies mask images or gradient masks. Use `mask-[<value>]` for image URLs or arbitrary CSS gradient functions. Linear, radial, and conic gradient masks are supported, with utilities to control angle, direction, stop positions, and colors. Directional gradient masks (`mask-t-from-`, `mask-x-from-`) allow masking specific edges or axes. Radial masks support various shapes, sizes, and explicit positioning. Negative angle values are supported for linear and conic gradients. Multiple gradient masks are combined using `mask-composite: intersect;` by default.

maskMode.label: Mask Mode
maskMode.description: Utilities for controlling an element's mask mode.
maskMode.notes: When using `mask-luminance` the luminance value of the mask determines visibility, so sticking with grayscale colors will produce the most predictable results. With `mask-alpha`, the opacity of the mask determines the visibility of the masked element.

maskOrigin.label: Mask Origin
maskOrigin.description: Utilities for controlling how an element's mask image is positioned relative to borders, padding, and content.
maskOrigin.notes: These utilities control the positioning area of an element's mask. The mask image can be anchored relative to the border box, padding box, content box, fill box, stroke box, or view box of the element.

maskPosition.label: Mask Position
maskPosition.description: Utilities for controlling the position of an element's mask image.
maskPosition.notes:
Controls the starting position of an element's mask image.
- Use keywords like `center`, `top`, `bottom right`.
- Supports arbitrary CSS position values (e.g., `[10px_20px]` or `[top_1rem_left_2rem]`).

maskRepeat.label: Mask Repeat
maskRepeat.description: Utilities for controlling the repetition of an element's mask image.
maskRepeat.notes: Control how an element's mask image repeats. `mask-repeat` repeats the mask image both vertically and horizontally. `mask-no-repeat` prevents repetition. Use `mask-repeat-x` or `mask-repeat-y` for axis-specific repetition. `mask-repeat-space` repeats the mask image without clipping, spacing images evenly if needed. `mask-repeat-round` repeats without clipping, stretching images to avoid gaps.

maskSize.label: Mask Size
maskSize.description: Utilities for controlling the size of an element's mask image.
maskSize.notes: Controls how the mask image is scaled relative to the mask layer. Use keywords like `auto` (default size), `cover` (scales to fill, cropping if necessary), or `contain` (scales to fit without cropping). Arbitrary values can be used to specify explicit width and height, e.g., `mask-size-[auto_100px]` or `mask-size-[50%_25%]`.

maskType.label: Mask Type
maskType.description: Utilities for controlling how an SVG mask is interpreted.
maskType.notes: When using `mask-type-luminance` the luminance value of the SVG mask determines visibility, so sticking with grayscale colors will produce the most predictable results. With `mask-alpha`, the opacity of the SVG mask determines the visibility of the masked element.

maxHeight.label: Max Height
maxHeight.description: Utilities for setting the maximum height of an element.
maxHeight.notes: Use `max-h-<number>` utilities to set a fixed maximum height based on the spacing scale. Use `max-h-<fraction>` or `max-h-full` for percentage-based maximum heights. Custom values can be defined using arbitrary value syntax like `max-h-[220px]`.

maxWidth.label: Max Width
maxWidth.description: Utilities for setting the maximum width of an element.
maxWidth.notes:
Sets the maximum width of an element.
- Fixed widths can be based on the spacing scale (e.g., `max-w-24`).
- Percentage-based widths use `full` or fractions (e.g., `max-w-1/2`).
- Semantic container sizes like `max-w-md` are available.
- Intrinsic widths (`min-content`, `max-content`, `fit-content`) are provided.
- Viewport unit based values (e.g., `max-w-dvh`).
- The standalone `container` utility (not `max-w-container`) sets breakpoint-specific max-widths and requires `mx-auto` and `px-<number>` for centering and padding.
- Arbitrary values are supported using `max-w-[<value>]` or `max-w-(<custom-property>)` (e.g., `max-w-[220px]`).

minHeight.label: Min Height
minHeight.description: Utilities for setting the minimum height of an element.
minHeight.notes: Sets the minimum height of an element. This utility supports values from the spacing scale, common fractions for percentages, and various viewport units. Use `min-h-[<value>]` for arbitrary values, or `min-h-(<custom-property>)` for CSS variables.

minWidth.label: Min-Width
minWidth.description: Utilities for setting the minimum width of an element.
minWidth.notes: Sets the minimum width of an element. This prevents the element from becoming smaller than a specified width. You can use values from the spacing scale, common fractions, predefined container sizes (like `sm` or `xl`), or arbitrary custom values. The `min-w` utility supports percentage-based widths like `min-w-1/2` and viewport-relative widths like `min-w-screen`.

mixBlendMode.label: Mix Blend Mode
mixBlendMode.description: Utilities for controlling how an element should blend with the background.
mixBlendMode.notes: Utilities like `mix-blend-multiply` control how an element's content and background blend with other content in the same stacking context. Use the `isolate` utility on a parent element to create a new stacking context, preventing blending with content behind it.

objectFit.label: Object Fit
objectFit.description: Utilities for controlling how a replaced element's content should be resized.
objectFit.notes: These utilities define how the content of ``, `

objectPosition.label: Object Position
objectPosition.description: Utilities for controlling how a replaced element's content should be positioned within its container.
objectPosition.notes: Controls how the content of replaced elements (like `` or `

opacity.label: Opacity
opacity.description: Utilities for controlling the opacity of an element.
opacity.notes: Controls the transparency of an element. Values range from 0 (fully transparent) to 100 (fully opaque). Supports arbitrary numeric values like `opacity-[.67]` or CSS custom properties `opacity-(var(--my-opacity))`.

order.label: Order
order.description: Utilities for controlling the order of flex and grid items.
order.notes: Controls the visual order of flex and grid items. Use `order-<number>` to explicitly set a sort order. `order-first` and `order-last` place items at the beginning or end. Use a negative prefix, e.g., `-order-1`, for negative values. Supports arbitrary values, including CSS custom properties or mathematical expressions.

outlineColor.label: Outline Color
outlineColor.description: Utilities for controlling the color of an element's outline.
outlineColor.notes: Outline color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any outline color by adding a forward slash followed by a percentage value (0-100). For example, `outline-red-500/50` applies a 50% opacity to the red-500 color. Arbitrary values can also be used, such as `outline-[currentColor]` or `outline-[rebeccapurple]`.

outlineOffset.label: Outline Offset
outlineOffset.description: Utilities for controlling the offset of an element's outline.
outlineOffset.notes: Controls the spacing between an element's outline and its border. Negative values pull the outline inwards. The default scale provides common offsets, but you can use arbitrary values for precise control.

outlineStyle.label: Outline Style
outlineStyle.description: Utilities for controlling the style of an element's outline.
outlineStyle.notes:
Use utilities like `outline-solid`, `outline-dashed`, `outline-dotted`, and `outline-double` to set the style of an element's outline. 
- `outline-hidden` hides the default browser outline on focused elements while preserving it in forced colors mode. It is highly recommended to apply your own focus styling for accessibility when using this utility. 
- `outline-none` completely removes the default browser outline on focused elements. It is highly recommended to apply your own focus styling for accessibility when using this utility.

outlineWidth.label: Outline Width
outlineWidth.description: Utilities for controlling the width of an element's outline.
outlineWidth.notes: Sets the width of an element's outline. The `outline` utility is a shorthand for `outline-1`. Use `outline-<number>` to apply a specific pixel width from the default scale, or use arbitrary values for custom lengths. Works well in conjunction with `outline-color` and `outline-style`.

overflowWrap.label: Overflow Wrap
overflowWrap.description: Utilities for controlling line breaks within words in an overflowing element.
overflowWrap.notes: Controls line breaks within words. `wrap-break-word` allows breaks between letters if needed. `wrap-anywhere` allows breaks between letters and influences the element's intrinsic size, which is useful in `flex` containers where it can prevent content from overflowing without needing `min-width: 0`. `wrap-normal` restricts breaks to natural wrapping points like spaces, hyphens, and punctuation.

overflow.label: Overflow
overflow.description: Utilities for controlling how an element handles content that is too large for the container.
overflow.notes: Controls how an element handles content that is too large. `overflow-visible` makes content visible even if it exceeds the element's bounds. `overflow-hidden` clips content that overflows. `overflow-clip` is similar to `hidden` but explicitly disallows scrollbars. `overflow-auto` adds scrollbars only when necessary, whereas `overflow-scroll` always adds them (though operating system settings may hide unnecessary scrollbars). Use `overflow-x-` and `overflow-y-` variants for controlling overflow along specific axes.

overscrollBehavior.label: Overscroll Behavior
overscrollBehavior.description: Utilities for controlling how the browser behaves when reaching the boundary of a scrolling area.
overscrollBehavior.notes:
Controls how the browser reacts when a scroll reaches the boundary of an element, preventing or allowing continued scrolling on parent elements ('scroll chaining') and 'bounce' effects. 
- `overscroll-auto`: Default behavior; allows scroll chaining and bounce. 
- `overscroll-contain`: Prevents scroll chaining, but preserves bounce. 
- `overscroll-none`: Prevents both scroll chaining and bounce.

padding.label: Padding
padding.description: Utilities for controlling an element's padding.
padding.notes:
Padding utilities control the space between an element's content and its border.
- Apply padding to all sides (`p-`), horizontal (`px-`), vertical (`py-`), or individual sides (`pt-`, `pr-`, `pb-`, `pl-`).
- Use `ps-` and `pe-` for logical inline-start/end padding, which respects text direction.
- Values typically map to the default spacing scale.
- `p-px` applies 1 pixel of padding.
- Custom values are supported using arbitrary value syntax, e.g., `p-[5px]`.

perspectiveOrigin.label: Perspective Origin
perspectiveOrigin.description: Utilities for controlling an element's perspective origin when placed in 3D space.
perspectiveOrigin.notes: The `perspective-origin` property defines the origin of the perspective for a 3D transformed element, effectively controlling the vanishing point. It accepts one or two values for X and Y coordinates. Use keywords like `top`, `bottom`, `left`, `right`, and their combinations. Arbitrary values can be percentages, lengths, or custom properties, for example `[200%_150%]`.

perspective.label: Perspective
perspective.description: Utilities for controlling an element's perspective when placed in 3D space.
perspective.notes: Controls how close or how far away the z-plane appears from the screen, similar to a camera's distance from an object. Use `perspective-none` to remove the perspective effect. Supports arbitrary length values, for example `[750px]`.

placeContent.label: Place Content
placeContent.description: Utilities for controlling how content is justified and aligned at the same time.
placeContent.notes: These utilities control the alignment and justification of content rows/columns in multi-line flex and grid containers simultaneously, along both the inline and block axes.

placeItems.label: Place Items
placeItems.description: Utilities for controlling how items are justified and aligned at the same time.
placeItems.notes: Controls how grid items are justified and aligned simultaneously within their grid areas. This utility affects both the horizontal and vertical alignment axes.

placeSelf.label: Place Self
placeSelf.description: Utilities for controlling how an individual item is justified and aligned at the same time.
placeSelf.notes:
These utilities influence both the horizontal and vertical alignment of a single item within its flex or grid container. 
- `place-self-auto` uses the container's `place-items` value. 
- `place-self-start` aligns an item to the start on both axes. 
- `place-self-end` aligns an item to the end on both axes. 
- `place-self-center` aligns an item at the center on both axes. 
- `place-self-stretch` stretches an item on both axes.

pointerEvents.label: Pointer Events
pointerEvents.description: Utilities for controlling whether an element responds to pointer events.
pointerEvents.notes: Use `pointer-events-none` to make an element ignore pointer events like `:hover` and `click`. Pointer events will still trigger on child elements and pass through to elements 'beneath' the target. Use `pointer-events-auto` to revert to default browser behavior.

position.label: Position
position.description: Utilities for controlling how an element is positioned in the document.
position.notes:
Controls how an element is positioned in the document:
- `static` elements ignore offsets and do not create a positioning context.
- `relative` elements define their offsets relative to their normal flow and create a positioning context for absolute children.
- `absolute` elements are removed from the normal flow, position relative to the nearest non-static parent, and create a positioning context.
- `fixed` elements position relative to the viewport.
- `sticky` elements act `relative` until a scroll threshold, then `fixed`, and create a positioning context.

resize.label: Resize
resize.description: Utilities for controlling how an element can be resized.
resize.notes:
Controls whether an element can be resized by the user. Drag the handle of a resizable element to observe its behavior. Key options include:
- `resize`: enables resizing in both horizontal and vertical directions.
- `resize-y`: enables vertical resizing.
- `resize-x`: enables horizontal resizing.
- `resize-none`: prevents any resizing.

rotate.label: Rotate
rotate.notes:
Rotates an element in 2D or 3D space. Key points:
- Default unit is degrees (`deg`).
- Use negative values for counter-clockwise rotation (e.g., `-rotate-45`).
- Use the X, Y, or Z variants (`rotate-x-`, `rotate-y-`) to rotate around a specific axis in 3D space.
- Arbitrary values can use other units like `rad`, `grad`, or `turn`.

scale.label: Scale
scale.notes:
Scales an element uniformly (2D) or along a specific axis (X, Y, Z). 
- Values are typically interpreted as percentages of the element's original size. 
- Negative values (e.g., `-scale-x-75`) can be used to mirror an element. 
- `scale-3d` sets scale for all three axes using CSS variables. 
- Arbitrary values (e.g., `scale-[1.7]`) allow for custom scale factors, which can be decimal numbers or percentages.

scrollBehavior.label: Scroll Behavior
scrollBehavior.description: Utilities for controlling the scroll behavior of an element.
scrollBehavior.notes: Controls the scroll behavior of an element, affecting only browser-triggered scroll events. Use `scroll-smooth` for smooth scrolling, and `scroll-auto` to revert to the default browser behavior.

scrollMargin.label: Scroll Margin
scrollMargin.description: Utilities for controlling the scroll offset around items in a snap container.
scrollMargin.notes: Sets the scroll offset around scroll-snap child elements, useful for preventing content from being obscured by fixed headers during scrolling. Values are derived from your configured `spacing` scale. Negative values can be applied by prefixing the class with a dash (e.g., `-scroll-ml-6`). Logical properties like `scroll-ms` (inline-start) and `scroll-me` (inline-end) adjust based on the text direction (LTR/RTL).

scrollPadding.label: Scroll Padding
scrollPadding.description: Utilities for controlling an element's scroll offset within a snap container.
scrollPadding.notes: Sets the scroll offset for an element within a snap container. Use `scroll-pt-<number>`, `scroll-pr-<number>`, `scroll-pb-<number>`, and `scroll-pl-<number>` for physical directions. Use `scroll-ps-<number>` and `scroll-pe-<number>` for logical properties that adapt to text direction. Negative values are supported by prefixing with a dash, e.g., `-scroll-ps-6`. Custom values can be defined using arbitrary value syntax, e.g., `scroll-pl-[24rem]`.

scrollSnapAlign.label: Scroll Snap Align
scrollSnapAlign.description: Utilities for controlling the scroll snap alignment of an element.
scrollSnapAlign.notes: Controls the alignment of a scroll snap area within its scroll container. Elements can snap to the `start`, `end`, or `center` of the container. Use `snap-align-none` to prevent snapping.

scrollSnapStop.label: Scroll Snap Stop
scrollSnapStop.description: Utilities for controlling whether you can skip past possible snap positions.
scrollSnapStop.notes: Use `snap-always` together with `snap-mandatory` to force a snap container to always stop on an element before the user can continue scrolling. Use `snap-normal` to allow a snap container to skip past possible scroll snap positions.

scrollSnapType.label: Scroll Snap Type
scrollSnapType.description: Utilities for controlling how strictly snap points are enforced in a snap container.
scrollSnapType.notes:
Controls how rigorously snap points are enforced in a scroll container. 
- `snap-x` enables horizontal snapping. 
- `snap-y` enables vertical snapping. 
- `snap-both` enables snapping on both axes. 
- `snap-mandatory` ensures the scroll container always lands on a snap point. 
- `snap-proximity` snaps to points that are close by. 
Requires `scroll-snap-align` on child elements to function correctly.

skew.label: Skew
skew.description: Utilities for skewing elements with transform.
skew.notes:
Skews an element along the X, Y, or both axes. Key points:
- Default unit is degrees (`deg`).
- Use negative values for counter-skew (e.g., `-skew-6`, `-skew-x-6`).
- Use the `skew-x-` and `skew-y-` variants to skew along a specific axis.
- Arbitrary values can use other units like `rad`, `grad`, or `turn`.

strokeWidth.label: Stroke Width
strokeWidth.description: Utilities for styling the stroke width of SVG elements.
strokeWidth.notes: Sets the width of the stroke on SVG elements. Numeric values like `stroke-1` and `stroke-2` are available. Arbitrary values can be defined using square brackets, e.g., `stroke-[1.5]` or `stroke-[var(--my-width)]` for custom lengths. This is useful for styling icon sets.

stroke.label: Stroke Color
stroke.description: Utilities for styling the stroke of SVG elements.
stroke.notes:
Utilities for coloring the stroke of SVG elements. 
- Use `stroke-current` to match the current text color.
- Supports all default Tailwind colors. 
- Custom colors can be defined using arbitrary values like `[#bada55]` or CSS variables like `(var(--my-color))`.

tableLayout.label: Table Layout
tableLayout.description: Utilities for controlling the table layout algorithm.
tableLayout.notes: Controls the table layout algorithm. `table-auto` automatically sizes columns to fit content. `table-fixed` uses fixed widths, ignoring content, and explicit column widths set in the first row apply to the entire table, with remaining space distributed evenly.

textAlign.label: Text Align
textAlign.description: Utilities for controlling the alignment of text.
textAlign.notes: Align text within an element using a fixed set of alignment options like left, center, right, and justify. These utilities correspond to the CSS `text-align` property.

textDecorationColor.label: Text Decoration Color
textDecorationColor.description: Utilities for controlling the color of text decorations.
textDecorationColor.notes: Text decoration color utilities are generated from your theme's `colors` object. You can add an opacity modifier to any text decoration color by adding a forward slash followed by a percentage value (0-100). For example, `decoration-sky-500/50` applies a 50% opacity. For custom values, use brackets like `decoration-[<value>]`, supporting various color formats like hex or RGB.

textDecorationLine.label: Text Decoration Line
textDecorationLine.description: Utilities for controlling the decoration of text.
textDecorationLine.notes: Controls the line decoration applied to text. Options include `underline`, `overline`, `line-through`, or `no-underline` to remove any decoration.

textDecorationStyle.label: Text Decoration Style
textDecorationStyle.description: Utilities for controlling the style of text decorations.
textDecorationStyle.notes: Utilities for controlling the style of text decorations, including `solid`, `double`, `dotted`, `dashed`, and `wavy`.

textDecorationThickness.label: Text Decoration Thickness
textDecorationThickness.description: Utilities for controlling the thickness of text decorations.
textDecorationThickness.notes: Controls the thickness of text decorations. Numeric values are in `px` by default. Also supports keywords like `auto` and `from-font`. Arbitrary values can be specified as CSS length units (e.g., `0.25rem`).

textIndent.label: Text Indent
textIndent.description: Utilities for controlling the amount of empty space shown before text in a block.
textIndent.notes: Sets the amount of empty space (indentation) before text in a block. Use negative values (e.g., `-indent-8`) for negative indentation. Supports `px` for 1 pixel and arbitrary values like `-[1.5rem]` or `-[50%]`.

textOverflow.label: Text Overflow
textOverflow.description: Utilities for controlling how the text of an element overflows.
textOverflow.notes: The `truncate` utility prevents text from wrapping and truncates overflowing text with an ellipsis. Use `text-ellipsis` to truncate overflowing text with an ellipsis. The `text-clip` utility truncates text at the limit of the content area, which is the default browser behavior.

textShadow.label: Text Shadow
textShadow.description: Utilities for controlling the shadow of a text element.
textShadow.notes: Applies a shadow effect to text. Use predefined sizes (`2xs`, `xs`, `sm`, `md`, `lg`) or `none` to remove. Adjust opacity with a forward slash followed by a percentage (e.g., `text-shadow-lg/50`). Custom colors can be applied using `text-shadow-<color>` or arbitrary values.

textTransform.label: Text Transform
textTransform.description: Utilities for controlling the capitalization of text.
textTransform.notes: Controls the capitalization of text. Options include `uppercase`, `lowercase`, `capitalize` (capitalizes the first letter of each word), and `normal-case` to reset casing. This is often used to override casing at different breakpoints.

textUnderlineOffset.label: Text Underline Offset
textUnderlineOffset.description: Utilities for controlling the offset of a text underline.
textUnderlineOffset.notes: Controls the distance between the text baseline and its underline. Numeric values are typically pixels; negative values are supported to move the underline above the baseline. Use `auto` for the browser's default. Arbitrary values support various length units like `px`, `rem`, or `em`.

textWrap.label: Text Wrap
textWrap.description: Utilities for controlling how text wraps within an element.
textWrap.notes: The `text-balance` utility is optimized for headings, as browsers typically limit text balancing to blocks of ~6 lines or less. `text-pretty` behavior varies by browser, often preventing orphans at the end of a text block, and may come at the expense of speed.

topRightBottomLeft.label: Top / Right / Bottom / Left
topRightBottomLeft.description: Utilities for controlling the placement of positioned elements.
topRightBottomLeft.notes: Controls the position of elements. Can be applied to all sides (`inset`), horizontally (`inset-x`), vertically (`inset-y`), or individually (`top`, `right`, `bottom`, `left`). Also supports logical properties (`start`, `end`) for text direction awareness. Values are based on your theme's `spacing` scale, and can be negative (e.g., `-top-4`). Also supports fractions, `px`, `full`, `auto`, and arbitrary values like `[3px]`.

touchAction.label: Touch Action
touchAction.description: Utilities for controlling how an element can be scrolled and zoomed on touchscreens.
touchAction.notes: Controls how an element responds to touch gestures, specifically panning (scrolling) and pinching (zooming). For example, `touch-none` disables all default touch actions, while `touch-pan-x` allows horizontal panning only.

transformOrigin.label: Transform Origin
transformOrigin.description: Utilities for specifying the origin for an element's transformations.
transformOrigin.notes: Sets the origin point for an element's transformations. This is the point around which rotations and scaling occur. You can use keywords like `center`, `top-left`, or `bottom`. For arbitrary values, specify X and Y coordinates, for example `origin-[33%_75%]` or a custom CSS variable like `origin-(var(--my-origin))`.

transform.label: Transform
transform.notes: Use `transform-gpu` to force hardware acceleration for better performance. Use `transform-cpu` to revert to CPU rendering if needed. Use `transform-none` to remove all transforms from an element. Arbitrary values accept any valid CSS transform function (e.g., `matrix`, `translate`, `rotate`, `scale`, `skew`).

transitionBehavior.label: Transition Behavior
transitionBehavior.description: Utilities to control the behavior of CSS transitions.
transitionBehavior.notes: Controls how CSS transitions behave, especially for discrete properties like `display` or `visibility`. `transition-discrete` allows these properties to transition, while `transition-normal` (the default) does not.

transitionDelay.label: Transition Delay
transitionDelay.description: Utilities for controlling the delay of CSS transitions.
transitionDelay.notes: Sets the delay for CSS transitions. Default values are in milliseconds (e.g., `delay-150` for 150ms). Arbitrary values can use other time units like seconds (e.g., `delay-[1s]`) or custom CSS properties.

transitionDuration.label: Transition Duration
transitionDuration.description: Utilities for controlling the duration of CSS transitions.
transitionDuration.notes: Utilities like `duration-150` and `duration-700` set the transition duration of an element in milliseconds. The `initial` keyword resets the property to its default value. For custom durations, use arbitrary values such as `duration-[1s]` or `duration-[var(--my-duration)]`.

transitionProperty.label: Transition Property
transitionProperty.description: Utilities for controlling which CSS properties transition.
transitionProperty.notes:
Controls which CSS properties are animated during transitions.
- Use predefined sets like `transition` (default properties), `transition-all`, `transition-colors`, or `transition-none`.
- Arbitrary values can be a single CSS property (e.g., `[height]`), or a comma-separated list (e.g., `[height, width]`).
- Custom CSS properties can be referenced, e.g., `-(var(--my-property))`.
- Supports `motion-reduce:transition-none` for reduced motion accessibility.

transitionTimingFunction.label: Transition Timing Function
transitionTimingFunction.description: Utilities for controlling the easing of CSS transitions.
transitionTimingFunction.notes: Controls the easing curve of an element's transition. Use preset keywords like `linear`, `in`, `out`, and `in-out`. You can define custom easing functions using CSS functions like `cubic-bezier()` or `steps()`, or by referencing custom CSS properties within square brackets.

translate.label: Translate
translate.notes:
Translates an element along the X, Y, or Z axis in 2D or 3D space.
- Supports numeric values (from the spacing scale), fractions (as percentages), `full` (100%), and `px` (1 pixel).
- Use negative values (e.g., `-translate-4`) for translation in the opposite direction.
- `translate-z` utilities require the `transform-3d` utility on the parent element.

userSelect.label: User Select
userSelect.description: Utilities for controlling whether the user can select text in an element.
userSelect.notes: Controls how users can select text within an element. Use `select-none` to prevent selection, `select-text` to allow default selection, `select-all` to select all text on a single click, and `select-auto` to use the browser's default behavior.

verticalAlign.label: Vertical Align
verticalAlign.description: Utilities for controlling the vertical alignment of an inline or table-cell box.
verticalAlign.notes: Controls the vertical alignment of inline or table-cell elements. This is useful for aligning text, images, or icons within a line of text or a table cell. Use keywords like `baseline`, `top`, `middle`, `bottom`, `text-top`, `text-bottom`, `sub`, and `super`. For custom offsets, arbitrary values with length units are supported, for example `align-[4px]` or `align-[2em]`.

visibility.label: Visibility
visibility.description: Utilities for controlling the visibility of an element.
visibility.notes: The `invisible` utility hides an element while maintaining its space in the document flow. The `collapse` utility hides table rows, row groups, columns, or column groups without affecting the table layout. `visible` is used to explicitly make an element visible, often to override `invisible` at different breakpoints.

whiteSpace.label: White Space
whiteSpace.description: Utilities for controlling an element's white-space property.
whiteSpace.notes: Controls how white space (spaces, tabs, newlines) is handled within an element, affecting text wrapping and whitespace collapsing. Options include normal wrapping, no wrapping, preserving spaces/newlines with or without wrapping, and allowing white space at the end of lines to wrap.

width.label: Width
width.description: Utilities for setting the width of an element.
width.notes:
Utilities for controlling the width of an element. 
- Fixed widths are based on the spacing scale (e.g., `w-24`).
- Percentage-based widths use fractions (e.g., `w-1/2`).
- Tailwind's container sizes (e.g., `w-md`) and viewport units (e.g., `w-screen`, `w-dvw`) are also available.
- `w-auto` resets the width.
- The `size-*` utilities set both width and height simultaneously (e.g., `size-16`, `size-full`).
- Supports arbitrary values like `w-[500px]` or CSS variables like `w-(some-var)`.

willChange.label: Will Change
willChange.description: Utilities for optimizing upcoming animations of elements that are expected to change.
willChange.notes: Instructs the browser to prepare for animations on specific properties, optimizing performance for upcoming changes. It's recommended to apply these utilities just before an element changes and remove them with `will-change-auto` shortly after. Use as a last resort for known performance problems, not in anticipation, as overuse can decrease performance. Supports arbitrary CSS property values.

wordBreak.label: Word Break
wordBreak.description: Utilities for controlling word breaks in an element.
wordBreak.notes: Controls how words break when reaching the end of a line. `break-normal` only breaks at normal word break points. `break-all` breaks whenever necessary, even in the middle of words. `break-keep` prevents line breaks for CJK text; for non-CJK text, it behaves like `break-normal`.

zIndex.label: Z-Index
zIndex.description: Utilities for controlling the stack order of an element.
zIndex.notes: Controls the stack order (or three-dimensional positioning) of an element. Use `z-<number>` for predefined values, `z-auto` for default behavior, or arbitrary values like `z-[<value>]` for custom stack orders. Negative values are supported, e.g., `-z-10`.
